subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Boeing's Safety Governance Failure
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Boeing's Safety Governance Failure.

hook.text: Two Boeing 737 MAX planes crashed, killing 346 people. The board had prioritized cost cuts over engineering.

buildup.text: Boeing merged with McDonnell Douglas and shifted from an engineering culture to a finance-driven one.

discovery.text: The MCAS system that caused the crashes was a cost-saving shortcut to avoid expensive pilot retraining.

twist.text: Internal emails showed engineers knew about the risks. Leadership dismissed their concerns as overblown.

climax.text: When governance prioritizes profit over safety in industries where lives are at stake, people die.

punchline.text: 346 lives lost. Cost cuts chose profits over safety.

quiz.question: What governance failure contributed to the Boeing 737 MAX crashes?
options: Prioritizing cost cuts and finance over engineering safety
Having too many engineers on the board
